To investigate the biochemical alterations associated with exhaustion, an in vitro model of CD8 + T cell exhaustion was established through chronic antigenic stimulation of murine OT-1 CD8 + T cells. Phenotypic, functional, metabolic, and transcriptional characterization confirmed the acquisition of an exhausted state.

title: Bidirectional interactions between gut microbiota and fluorochemical biotransformation and bioactivity

s2.tldr: An integrated ex vivo, in vitro, and in silico approach is established for assessing the bidirectional interactions between fluorinated chemicals and the gut microbiome, establishing an integrated ex vivo, in vitro, and in silico approach.

abstractExcerpt: Fluorinated chemicals are increasingly prevalent in pharmaceuticals and agrochemicals, yet their influence on the human gut microbiome and the potential for microbial biotransformation to alter therapeutic and toxicological profiles remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated the bidirectional relationship between 15 structurally diverse fluorinated chemicals and the gut microbiota by using an ex vivo high-throughput fermentation system.

title: Structure-Independent Genetic Algorithm-Based Molecular Optimization Using Pocket-Aware Molecular Representations
abstractExcerpt: De novo molecular design typically depends on target structures or ligand poses, limiting its applicability when structural information is unavailable. Here, we introduce the pocket-aware molecular representation-guided genetic algorithm (PAMR-GA), a target-structure-independent molecular optimization framework that learns pocket-aware representations from structure–activity relationship (SAR) data using only molecular structures represented as SMILES strings and experimental pIC50 values.

title: Leveraging Machine Learning for Accelerated Electrode-Electrolyte Interface Design in Rechargeable Li-Based Batteries

s2.tldr: Future trajectories centered on multiscale materials simulation, multimodal modeling, and intelligent platform establishment to overcome persistent challenges are outlined, aiming at catalyzing the rational design of highly stable lithium electrode-electrolyte interface for long-lasting rechargeable LMBs.

abstractExcerpt: Due to their high specific energy, lithium-metal batteries (LMBs) are widely regarded as the promising next-generation energy storage devices. Nevertheless, their practical applications are plagued by the challenges of irregular deposition and dissolution, coupled with the high chemical reactivity of lithium electrodes. Extensive research has focused on the stabilization of electrode-electrolyte interfaces as the key strategy to achieve improved battery performance.

title: Predicting Water-Induced Demixing of Ionic Liquid Mixtures with Associative Electrolyte PC-SAFT
abstractExcerpt: Ionic liquids (ILs) can be mixed with other ILs to fine-tune their physicochemical properties. While ILs have been long considered inseparable, recent studies have demonstrated that the controlled addition of water enables the selective recovery of the constituent salts, opening new opportunities for sustainable IL recycling and separation. The rational design of these IL mixtures remains challenging due to the lack of predictive models capable of accurately capturing the interplay between competing short- and long-range interactions in IL-based systems, particularly in multi-IL systems…

s2.tldr: The new MPI+OpenMP+GPU parallelization substantially accelerates electron-phonon coupling and electron dynamics calculations, providing a scalable computational framework and a foundation for future large-scale studies in both conventional and quantum materials.

abstractExcerpt: The Boltzmann transport equation (BTE) with electron-phonon ( e -ph) interactions computed from first principles is widely used to study electronic transport and nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. This challenge makes it difficult to study materials with large unit cells and to achieve high resolution in momentum space.

abstractExcerpt: This study investigates the microstructural evolution of the powder metallurgical high-speed steel PM HS 3-3-4 during isothermal holding within the transformation gap between pearlite and bainite formation. The focus is on the mechanism of carbide spheroidization and the proposed formation of a chemically graded carbide rim. The heat treatments were carried out in a quenching dilatometer, enabling precise control of the thermal cycles and isothermal holding conditions.

title: Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Phononic Crystals for Targeted Elastic Wave Bandgap
abstractExcerpt: Phononic crystals are periodic elastic structures that exhibit frequency bandgaps within which elastic waves cannot propagate. The formation and width of these bandgaps depend on the spatial distribution of material properties within periodic phononic unit cells. In this work, we propose novel topology optimization formulations to achieve multi-material design of phononic crystals for bandgap optimization at targeted frequencies, where we discover the influence of spatially varying properties of base materials on the band structures that block and permit elastic wave propagation.

title: Probing the sequence variability tolerance in a de novo α-helical barrel biocatalyst

s2.tldr: Deep learning based and classic computational protein design is combined to modify and optimize de novo α-helical barrel biocatalysts to provide new insights and possibilities for the further engineering of functional de novo α-helical barrels, their ability to withstand dramatically large sequence changes and their broader application in biocatalysis and biotechnology.

abstractExcerpt: De novo-designed enzymes have recently achieved high catalytic activity and stereoselectivity while demonstrating exceptional thermostability in entirely novel protein scaffolds. Among these, -helical barrel protein scaffolds are attractive structures for biocatalysis due to their structural simplicity, high thermostability, and rationalizable sequence patterning.

title: CDGA: A Host-Based Alignment and Descriptor Analysis Tool for Cyclodextrin Inclusion Complexes
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

s2.tldr: CDGA was validated using controlled geometrical and chemical modifications and cross-docked and redocked poses generated for conformationally diverse native cyclodextrins, demonstrating robust and reproducible descriptor calculation despite differences in atom ordering, bond representation, host orientation, and molecular file generation.

abstractExcerpt: Computational studies of cyclodextrin inclusion complexes are widespread; however, quantitative comparison of host–guest geometries remains difficult because native cyclodextrins are cyclic and pseudosymmetric, with chemically equivalent glucose units and no unique structural anchor for conventional atom-to-atom mapping. Consequently, RMSD values, guest orientations, and pose comparisons may depend on arbitrary atom numbering, molecular file representation, or software-specific alignment procedures rather than on genuine structural differences.

title: Morphology-Property Interplay in Chemo-Mechanics of Ion-Intercalation Active Particles
abstractExcerpt: Morphology, material property, and mechanical constraint jointly govern the chemo-mechanical behavior of ion-intercalation particles, yet their coupled effects remain insufficiently understood. Here we establish a thermodynamically consistent single-particle framework and combine analytical solutions with multiphysics simulations to determine how these factors regulate lithiation and stress generation.

abstractExcerpt: Recovering complete phase sets from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) is challenging when weak-phase peaks overlap stronger signals. A natural strategy is to identify phases iteratively, removing the contribution of each identified phase from the observed pattern before predicting the next. However, even after a phase is correctly identified, misestimating its contribution can distort the residual and cause subsequent errors. We introduce PhaseMatcher, an autoregressive framework for complete phase-set identification with physics-guided spectral decomposition.

The 6.1% volume shrinkage in Bi0.82Nd0.18CoO3 is the largest ever observed in Pb-free NTE materials.

title: OrbitChem: An Integrated Machine Learning and Physics-Based Platform for Space-Grade Molecular Design and Spacecraft Material Qualification
abstractExcerpt: The design of molecular absorbers for space-based photovoltaic applications demands simultaneous optimisation across quantum-chemical properties (bandgap, absorption efficiency), spacecraft material qualification standards (outgassing, radiation stability, thermal cycling fatigue), and mission-specific environmental constraints. No existing computational tool addresses these three domains in a single integrated pipeline.

title: Transition-state lattice modes and the breakdown of adiabatic tunneling for hydrogen and deuterium in bcc Nb
abstractExcerpt: Interstitial hydrogen and deuterium in body-centered-cubic metals constitute archetypal quantum tunneling systems. Their relevance has been renewed by the connection between hydrogenic tunneling in Nb and defect-induced decoherence in superconducting qubits, motivating a predictive microscopic theory. Existing theoretical treatments invoke an adiabatic separation between the light interstitial and the host lattice, an assumption whose validity has not been rigorously established for hydrogenic species.

title: Hematopoietic stem cell aging: a review of transcriptional and multi-omics insights and potential paths for AI integration

s2.tldr: A curated, centralized, interactive database is proposed as a community resource to integrate multi-omics data and artificial intelligence-driven approaches to enhance understanding and potential interventions for age-related hematopoietic disorders.

abstractExcerpt: Hematopoietic stem cell (HSC) aging underlies age-related immune decline, anemia and increased risk of hematologic malignancies, including clonal hematopoiesis and leukemia. Many available microarray and bulk RNA sequencing studies have elucidated conserved transcriptional hallmarks, such as myeloid bias, inflammation dysregulation, and self-renewal reinforcement in aged HSCs across mouse and human models. Here, we review key publicly available transcriptome and epigenome datasets from landmark studies, highlighting their contributions to defining HSC molecular aging signatures.

title: An accurate full-dimensional potential energy surface of N2 + H2O for high-energy collisions
abstractExcerpt: A full-dimensional potential energy surface (PES) is developed for H2O–N2 collisions to enable state-resolved simulations under high-temperature, nonequilibrium conditions. A total of 81,447 configurations were calculated using coupled-cluster singles, doubles, and perturbative triples with explicit correlation [CCSD(T)-F12a] and the aug-cc-pVTZ basis set; the resulting energies were fitted using the permutation invariant polynomial-neural network (PIP-NN) approach.
